101: MoMo -the blood taker- by Akira Sugito (Seven Seas) is a dark supernatural mystery with a thread of romance running through it. Tokyo is gripped by a string of murders in which the victims are drained of blood, and rumors of vampires are spreading. Detective Keigo Mikogami is hunting the killer he calls "The Man With Two Faces" to avenge his murdered lover, and his search draws the attention of a mysterious silver-haired girl. It's a good fit for readers who like moody vampire stories with a detective's edge.
102: A-DO by Jaku Amano (Kodansha) is a sci-fi action story with a streetwise heart. In a near-future Japan tense with anti-immigrant protests, Riko, a restless young woman who can't hold down a job, saves a boy named Eito from a speeding truck and ends up looking after him. When an army sniper takes a shot at Eito, plant-like tendrils burst from his arm to stop the bullet. It's a fresh pick for readers who like unlikely guardians and mysterious kids with strange powers.
103: Tank Chair by Manabu Yashiro (Kodansha) is a gritty, high-energy action story. On Guicheng Island, known as the most dangerous town in the universe, gangs fight for power with genetic doping. Young Shizuka takes on risky assassination jobs, but it's her brother Nagi who does the fighting: he took a bullet to protect her and now lies comatose in a heavily armed wheelchair, waking only when threatened. It's a great pick for fans of over-the-top battles and fierce sibling bonds.
104: Gazing at the Star Next Door by Ammitsu (Kodansha) is a sweet, heartfelt shojo romance. Chiaki Amano has loved her childhood friend Subaru Hiiragi for as long as she can remember, but now he's an actor whose fame keeps growing. She tells herself it's time to give up on him, yet because they still spend so much time together, her feelings refuse to fade. It's a lovely read for anyone who enjoys slow-burn romances and childhood friends on the edge of something more.
105: Moon Boy by Lee YoungYou (Ice Kunion) is a fantasy romance manhwa rooted in Korean folklore. Years ago, Myung-Ee Joo met a classmate whose eyes turned red under the moon, just like hers, and then he vanished from everyone's memory but her own. Now in high school, she finds him on the student council with no memory of her, and learns she is an Earth Rabbit, a descendant of the moon rabbits hunted by the Fox tribe. It's a charming pick for readers who like folklore-flavored school fantasy.
106: Arcana by So-Young Lee (Tokyopop) is a classic fantasy adventure manhwa. Inez is an orphan with the rare gift of speaking to every kind of creature, and she is told she is destined to be the chosen one. Summoned to the capital, she learns she must find and bring back the guardian dragon that keeps the kingdom's fragile peace safe from a demon race waiting in the shadows. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy chosen-one quests with gentle heroines and beautiful fantasy art.
107: Never Give Up! by Hiromu Mutou (Tokyopop) is a lighthearted shojo romantic comedy set in the modeling world. Fifteen-year-old Kiri has loved her childhood friend Tohya for years and planned to confess once she became beautiful enough. When Tohya is scouted as a model, Kiri, who has a boyish look, poses as a male model named Tatsuki so she can stay close and watch over him, and both of them end up unexpectedly famous. It's a fun pick for fans of disguise comedies and devoted heroines.
109: Hour of the Zombie by Tsukasa Saimura (Seven Seas) is a tense, unusual take on zombie horror. Akira Nikaidou is going through an ordinary school day with his friends and his crush, Kurumi, when his classmates suddenly turn into zombies. Then, strangely, the zombies stop attacking, leaving Akira and the other survivors to wonder what happens next. It's a good pick for horror readers who like slow-building dread and survival stories that don't follow the usual rules.
108: High School Girls by Towa Oshima (Comics One) is a rowdy, good-natured school comedy. Eriko and her friends Yuma and Ayano are thrilled to start high school, but sneaking a tour of their new all-girls school before the opening ceremony shows them it isn't quite what they imagined. Soon they've gathered a lively circle of new friends, from an attention-loving aspiring actress to a petite girl with very odd solutions to every problem. It's a fun pick for readers who like frank, silly slice-of-life humor.
110: I Hate You More Than Anyone! by Banri Hidaka (CMX) is a warm shojo romantic comedy. Kazuha Akiyoshi is the responsible eldest daughter of a big family and attends an all-girls high school with her best friend, Senko. During the school festival, she catches the eye of Maki Sugimoto, a hairstylist, but her growing feelings for him put a strain on her friendship, because Senko has a crush on him too. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy ensemble romances with plenty of heart.
111: Pandora Seven by Yuta Kayashima (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure with a big heart. Lia is the only humania on her island, but despite her nonhuman traits she lives happily with her mother and friends. That peace ends when humans arrive and attack the people she loves, and after she opens a mysterious box, Lia sets out alone on a quest to save them. It's a good pick for readers who like determined young heroes and quests built around a world-changing secret.
116: Platinum Garden by Maki Fujita (Tokyopop) is a shojo romance with a supernatural twist. When Kazura Enomoto's grandfather dies, he leaves her to Mizuki Magahara, the son of a wealthy family, to settle his debts. Kazura expects to work as a servant but learns she is meant to be Mizuki's fiancee instead. As she adjusts to his elite school, she begins to uncover the Magahara family's unusual secret. It's a nice fit for readers who enjoy arranged-engagement romances with a touch of mystery.
119: Reborn as a Barrier Master by Naotaro Kataoka (Seven Seas) is an isekai fantasy about making a life from nothing. Overworked 34-year-old Tamotsu Kubo wakes up in another world as a six-year-old with hidden Barrier Master skills, only to land on the auction block of a slave market. When no one bids, Marquess Basam rescues him and raises him as his personal Barrier Master under the name Linus. It's a good pick for fans of underdog isekai stories where talent grows through hard work.
120: Ultra Cute by Nami Akimoto (Tokyopop) is a bubbly shojo romantic comedy. Best friends Ami and Noa have been rivals since kindergarten, always chasing the same boys and never landing any of them. At fifteen they meet Tamon and Hiro, and for once they like different guys. The boys, though, are playing a game of their own, and a meddling ex-girlfriend and an odd teacher are ready to make things harder. It's a fun, light read for fans of high-energy school romance.
121: Unholy Blood by Lina Lim (Ize Press) is a stylish supernatural action thriller in full color. Hayan Park is a pureblood vampire who just wants a quiet life, but ever since vampire-human hybrids appeared a decade ago, the world has grown dangerous and she has to keep her nature hidden. When a professor she cares about is murdered and a police captain starts to suspect her, she may have to use her true powers. It's a great pick for readers who like sleek vampire stories with a mystery at the core.
122: Lights Out by Myung-Jin Lee (Tokyopop) is a high school manhwa that mixes action, comedy, and a bit of romance, from the creator of Ragnarok. Nam Gung Geon is a hot-tempered transfer student with a violent streak, but his life starts to change after he meets Min Seung-Ah, whose grandfather owns an inn called Fate. Soon he's making real friends and finding his footing at school. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy tough-guy heroes with a softer side.
